points.description: States the core difference: a constructor is called automatically when an object is created, whereas a function must be called explicitly. (A mention that constructors have no return type while functions do also counts toward this point.)
points.partial_credit: Award 2-3 marks if only one half is given, e.g. only the return-type difference or only that constructors run on object creation, or if the idea is vague or incomplete.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying a constructor runs automatically when an object is created while a function must be called explicitly. Any wording is fine, and the return-type difference is accepted as a correct extra or as the other half of the fact. Give part marks for a partial or vague statement, and 0 for answers that only describe what a constructor or function is without any difference.
